title: Taco Seasoning — Old El Paso Style (From Scratch)
description: A homemade taco seasoning that replicates the Old El Paso packet blend — but fresher, deeper, and completely under your control. One batch equals roughly one standard 35 g packet.

method.instruction: Measure all spices into a small bowl.
Use immediately or store in an airtight jar. Label with the date. Keeps well for up to 6 months.

notes.title: Old El Paso Comparison
notes.content: The commercial packet uses corn starch, chili pepper, maltodextrin, salt, spice, and onion powder. This blend delivers the same flavour with proper depth from fresh ground cumin and real paprika. The plain flour acts as the thickener.

notes.title: Heat Level
notes.content: 1 tsp chili powder gives mild-medium heat matching the standard packet. Reduce to 1/2 tsp for mild, increase to 1 1/2 to 2 tsp for hot. A pinch of cayenne adds extra kick.

notes.title: Trevor's Touch
notes.content: For notably better flavour, toast whole cumin seeds and coriander seeds in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until fragrant, then grind fresh. It transforms the depth of the blend completely.

notes.title: Scaling Up
notes.content: To make a bulk jar, multiply everything by 4 or 6 and store. Use 2 heaped tablespoons per 500 g of mince — same as the packet instructions.
